title: A separable root of a polynomial with p-th power coefficients is a p-th power
statement: Let $p$ be a prime, $E$ a field of characteristic $p$ and $L/E$ a separable algebraic extension [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Let $\alpha\in L$ and let $P\in E[T]$ be a polynomial such that (a) $P(\alpha)=0$, (b) $P$ has pairwise distinct roots in an algebraic closure of $E$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and (c) every coefficient of $P$ is a $p$-th power of an element of $E$. Then $\alpha=\alpha'^p$ for some $\alpha'\in L$.

source.place: Fields, Lemma Tag 031V (lemma-pth-root, line 3747), part (2), and its proof (uses Lemma lemma-take-pth-root)

mathlib_searches.query: if alpha is separable over K, root of polynomial with distinct roots whose coefficients are p-th powers, then alpha is a p-th power
In characteristic p, if L/K is separable algebraic and α in L is a root of a polynomial with distinct roots whose coefficients are p-th powers in K, then α is a p-th power in L
